s7.p1: ![ico-20 warn] Each function call results in the creation of a new execution context.
s7.p2: The execution context is created before code execution begins.
s7.p4: While the function execution is not completed, its context will be active.
s7.p5: Since functions can call each other, their context is pushed onto the stack
s7.p7: The top of this stack will always be the current execution context.
s7.p8: What will be present in this context?
s8.p1: ^^When a function is called, it is activated^^
s8.p2: ^^It needs somewhere to safely “place” its data with which it will work^^
s8.p3: ^^In addition to the arguments a function receives when called, it can have its own internal data needed for temporarily storing intermediate computation results.^^
s8.p4: When a function is called, an object is created containing all the necessary variables.
s8.p6: ⟦f37⟧ contains the function arguments and all variables declared inside the function (including functions)
s8.p7: ^^therefore it is also called _variable object_ or _activation object_^^
s8.p8: ^^Thus, the activation object can be compared to a locker for storing the “personal belongings” of the function^^
s8.p9: ^^![ico-20 warn] It's impossible to access activation object^^
s9.p7: ![ico-20 warn] Please note that all internal variables and nested functions are declared before the code starts executing, regardless of the order in which they appear in the code.
s9.p8: ![ico-20 warn] But assignment of values ​​to variables occurs when the code starts executing.
s9.p9: This results in **hoisting** of variable and function declarations
s9.p11: ^^Although the declaration of variables **_⟦f40⟧_** and **_⟦f41⟧_** appears in the code after the ⟦f42⟧ statement, during the creation of the execution context, an activation object (Lexical Environment) will be formed in the first stage, and all variables declared within the function will be included in this object.^^
s9.p12: ^^Thus, the declaration of variables **_⟦f43⟧_** and **_⟦f44⟧_** will take place before the code execution starts.^^
s9.p13: ^^However, the values will be assigned to variables only at the the second stage, and the code will be executed sequentially.^^
s9.p14: ^^Therefore, at the time of executing the code `console.log(x)`, the value of the variable **_⟦f45⟧_** will not be defined, so ⟦f46⟧' will be printed in the console.^^

s10.p1: **⟦f55⟧** limits the access and visibility of variable and function identifiers.
s10.p2: ^^Imagine two people named Sasha: 👨‍💼 a guy and 🙎 a girl.^^
s10.p4: ^^and guy Sasha 👨‍💼 is in the first room,^^
s10.p5: ^^while girl Sasha 🙎 is in the second one.^^
s10.p7: ^^If we ask the observer in the first room: _"Who is Sasha?"_,^^
s10.p9: ^^Asking a similar question to the observer in the second room, we'll get the answer: _"The girl"_ 🙎^^
s10.p10: ^^This happens because each room has its own scope.^^
s10.p11: ^^However, the scope of nested functions will be somewhat different.^^
s10.p12: ^^Let's assume that nested functions are boxes with walls made of tinted glass.^^
s10.p13: ^^Our function-boxes are nested within each other, like nesting dolls:^^
s10.p14: ^^the second box is inside the first one,^^
s10.p15: ^^the third one is inside the second one, and so on...^^
s10.p16: ^^The observer in box 2 will not only see the contents of box 2,^^
s10.p18: ^^and the room where all the boxes are located,^^
s10.p19: ^^but he cannot see the contents of box 3,^^
s10.p20: ^^although the observer in box 3 can see them perfectly...^^
s10.p21: ^^as well as the observers in all other boxes^^
s10.p23: ^^Thus, if a function refers to a variable, it will first look for this variable in its "personal belongings cabinet", and if it doesn't find it, it won't hesitate to "borrow" this variable from the outer room where it is located. ^^
s10.p24: ^^![ico-20 warn] All nested each other outer "cabinets" represent a ![ico-20 pin] chain of function scopes, which is part of its ![ico-20 pin] **execution context**.^^
s10.p26: ^^The variable **⟦f56⟧**   is declared in the global scope, where the function **⟦f57⟧** is also declared.^^
s10.p27: ^^The variable **⟦f58⟧** is assigned the value 1 upon declaration.^^
s10.p28: ^^Since there is no declaration of the variable **⟦f59⟧** inside the **⟦f60⟧** function, when the execution context of the **⟦f61⟧** function is formed, this variable will not be included to the activation object ("personal belongings cabinet") of the **⟦f62⟧** function.^^
s10.p31: ^^the **⟦f63⟧** function, not finding such a variable in its own "room", refers to the external "room" where such a variable exists, and it will be assigned the value 10.^^
s10.p32: ^^Thus, for each execution context, there exists its own chain of scopes.^^
s10.p33: ^^The scope chain includes the scopes of all previous contexts in the stack.^^
s10.p36: ^^This example demonstrates how the **hoisting** mechanism works.^^
s10.p37: ^^The variable **⟦f64⟧** is declared in the global scope with a value of 1.^^
s10.p38: ^^Inside the **⟦f65⟧** function, after the return statement, the **⟦f66⟧** function is declared.^^
s10.p39: After the execution of the showSample function is completed, its context will be "unmounted", and the global context will become active again, where the sample variable has a value of 1.
s10.p40: ^^At first glance, when the code is executed sequentially, this declaration shouldn't work because the ⟦f67⟧ statement is placed above it.^^
s10.p41: ^^However, all declarations are gathered into the activation object before the code starts executing.^^
s10.p42: ^^Therefore, by the time the code of the **⟦f68⟧** function starts executing, the **⟦f69⟧** function will already be declared and will be safely located in the ⟦f70⟧ of the **⟦f71⟧** function.^^
s10.p43: ^^Thanks to this, variable and function declarations "hoist" to the scope of their "parent" (in our case, the "parent" is the **⟦f72⟧** function).^^
s10.p44: ^^This is confirmed by logging the **⟦f73⟧** variable to the console.^^
s10.p45: ^^After the execution of the **⟦f74⟧** function is completed, its context will be "unmounted", and the global context will become active again, where the sample variable has a value of 1.^^
